text: I thought it necessary that I do exactly the contrary, and that I reject as absolutely false everything in which I could imagine the slightest doubt, in order to see whether, after this, anything would remain in my belief that was entirely indubitable. Thus, because our senses sometimes deceive us, I resolved to suppose that nothing was such as they make us imagine it to be. And because there are men who err in reasoning, even concerning the simplest matters of geometry, and commit paralogisms, judging that I was subject to error as much as any other, I rejected as false all the reasons I had previously taken for demonstrations. And finally, considering that all the same thoughts we have when awake can also come to us when we sleep, without any of them being true at that time, I resolved to pretend that all the things that had ever entered my mind were no more true than the illusions of my dreams. But immediately afterward, I noticed that, while I wished in this way to think that everything was false, it was necessary that I, who was thinking this, be something. And observing that this truth: I think, therefore I am, was so firm and so assured that all the most extravagant suppositions of the skeptics were incapable of shaking it, I judged that I could accept it, without scruple, as the first principle of the philosophy I was seeking.

I resolved to reject as false everything in which I could imagine the slightest doubt, to see whether anything would remain entirely indubitable. Because our senses sometimes deceive us, I supposed nothing was as they make us imagine. Because men err in reasoning, even in simple geometry, I rejected as false all reasons I had taken for demonstrations. Considering that waking thoughts can also come in sleep, I pretended all things in my mind were no more true than dreams. But I noticed that while I thought everything false, I who was thinking must be something. I think, therefore I am — this truth was so assured that I accepted it as the first principle of my philosophy.

I set out to reject everything doubtful. I doubted my senses, for they deceive. I doubted all reasoning, for men commit errors. I supposed everything I experienced might be a dream. But while doubting everything, I could not doubt that I was thinking. I think, therefore I am — the first indubitable principle of philosophy.
Doubt everything: senses deceive, reasoning errs, waking may be dreaming. But even in universal doubt, to doubt is to think. I think, therefore I am. This is the first principle of philosophy.
